content:
samir: cloudsec-bot flagged a public S3 bucket: redwood-logs-prod-backup. ACL=PUBLIC-READ. Scanner found immediate exposure.
sec-bot: [automated] detection_id=cs-20240613-0925, severity=high, rule=s3-public-acl.
priya: ack. paging oncall. anyone oncall for infra? @julia?
julia: i'm oncall, investigating now. can someone share who owns that bucket?
samir: tags show owner: infra-logging-service (service-account: logging-agent). No recent deploys from that service in last 24h per deploy-bot.
noah: jumping in. first capture: listing public ACLs and objects. running a quick list -- only a handful of objects, mostly gz logs. not seeing huge volumes.
julia: good. containment plan: 1) make bucket private (ACL + public access block), 2) snapshot current object list + sizes + last modified, 3) search CloudTrail for GET/GETOBJECT events, 4) rotate keys for logging-agent if suspicious.
priya: agree. please run commands and paste outputs. keep changes minimal and reversible.
noah: running containment now.
noah: ```bash
aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-logs-prod-backup --acl private
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket redwood-logs-prod-backup --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true
```
noah: applied. AWS returned 200 for both. bucket ACL now private. PublicAccessBlock in place.
samir: thanks. can you also remove any bucket policy that allows "Principal": "*"?
julia: listing policy... found a legacy policy left by a one-off script from 2022 that allowed GetObject for everyone. removing it now.
julia: ```bash
aws s3api delete-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-logs-prod-backup
```
julia: policy removed.
noah: snapshotting object list and checksums now and uploading to secure incident bucket.
noah: `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-logs-prod-backup --recursive --human-readable > /tmp/backup-list.txt && md5sum /tmp/backup-list.txt`
noah: snapshot saved and uploaded to s3://sec-incident-2024/backups/redwood-logs-prod-backup-1718273945.txt
priya: next: CloudTrail search for recent GET object events against this bucket.
samir: running quick lookup.
samir: ```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:s3:::redwood-logs-prod-backup --start-time 2024-06-12T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-06-13T12:00:00Z
```
samir: found 3 GetObject events in the last 36h. IPs: 18.206.12.45, 3.120.98.14, 54.210.23.11 (all EC2 ranges).
julia: are those internal AWS IPs or external customers? cross-refing with VPC NAT ranges... looks external.
noah: timeline: the GetObject calls coincide with an automated backup job that previously used a pre-signed URL generator (bug: generator accidentally created public ACL). The job runs from a logging-agent, using service-account credentials.
priya: immediate mitigation done. next: rotate the logging-agent keys and revoke any active sessions. who has IAM permissions? @julia can you rotate and create replacement creds pinned to restricted policy?
julia: creating new role with limited s3 PutObject/List permissions only to the exact prefix. will attach and rotate.
julia: ```bash
# create new policy (JSON inline)
aws iam create-policy --policy-name LoggingAgentRestrictedS3 --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:PutObject","s3:ListBucket"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-logs-prod-backup","arn:aws:s3:::redwood-logs-prod-backup/*"],"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"s3:prefix":"incoming/"}}}]}'
# attach to role and rotate keys
```
julia: rotated keys and invalidated old credentials via `aws iam delete-access-key` for the affected user. new credentials pushed to secrets manager and deployed to logging-agent via existing secret rotation flow.
priya: good. we've contained exposure and rotated creds. next: check for data exfil (downloads). samir can you run Athena/CloudTrail logs to see if any large GET ranges or downloads from suspicious IPs?
samir: running an ad-hoc Athena query on CloudTrail logs for GetObject and bytes returned... will take ~5m.
samir: query shows three GETs but small sizes (log fragments ~30-40KB each). no bulk download pattern.
noah: cross-check with CDN or third-party logs? nothing else shows access.
julia: we should assume low impact but still treat as incident. opening incident ticket and slack #incidents. tagging product security and legal for notification.
priya: please add timeline and actions to incident ticket. also schedule a 1-hr postmortem tomorrow. action items: automated IAM sweep for public ACLs, add bucket policy guardrails (deny public), ensure infra provisioning tests fail if bucket created with public ACL, add runtime alert to block public ACLs immediately.
noah: logging-agent script was the root cause (legacy presigned + ACL). adding code fix and tests now. PR will block granting public ACLs.
julia: recommend additional controls: enable default bucket encryption, enforce BlockPublicAccess at org level, enable S3 access logging to centralized bucket, and add a periodic scan runbook.
samir: agreed. adding to backlog and will make PR for org SCP to block public buckets in prod accounts.
priya: comms: draft internal note for leadership: minimal data exposure, no PII, logs only, three GETs from external IPs, containment done, keys rotated, follow-ups scheduled. I'll draft and share.
julia: leaving final checklist here: 1) containment performed (ACL+policy+public block) ✅ 2) keys rotated ✅ 3) snapshot + evidence uploaded ✅ 4) CloudTrail analysis => limited downloads ✅ 5) incident ticket and PM scheduled ✅
noah: adding automated rule to infra-templates to set s3:BlockPublicAcls by default and fail CI if absent.
priya: nice work team. will queue a retro and list follow-ups: org SCP, CI guardrails, runtime detections, and owner cleanup for legacy scripts.
samir: closing this thread when PRs are merged. tagging @sec-bot to add incident to monthly security report. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: [automated] incident created: INC-2024-0623-002, severity=low-medium, owner=eng-security, runbook=investigate-s3-public, evidence_s3=s3://sec-incident-2024/backups/redwood-logs-prod-backup-1718273945.txt
